1.why: All text uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height, though letter spacing appears default rather than notably generous.

2.why: Instructions are short sentence-case lines with no italics or dense paragraphs; the only all-caps text is the small 'STEP 1 OF 5' label.

3.why: The single-column layout with full-width fields and button reads cleanly at the narrow mobile width shown, though the empty black logs panel adds dead space.

4.why: The only instructions are one- or two-sentence plain-language lines such as 'Confirm your bank account details to protect higher-value payments.'

5.why: Example inputs are shown directly in the fields ('marcus@example.test', '+15551234567') and reinforced by 'Assessment demo: use the displayed example details.'

6.why: No screen contains more than a couple of short lines of text, so the user never has to read a long block to proceed.

7.why: No long codes or secrets are ever displayed or made copyable; the flow stalls at step 1 so OTP and recovery codes never appear.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered on any of the four screens.

9.why: The form has no password field and shows no visible autocomplete or password-manager affordances, so such support is not demonstrated.

10.why: The 'STEP 1 OF 5' label, bold heading, and full-width blue 'Continue securely' button make the current step and primary action unmistakable.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one primary action ('Continue securely') with no competing buttons.

12.why: After submitting, the system only shows 'Unable to sign in with those details.' without stating what happens next, and no success feedback is ever reachable.

13.why: The sign-in form can be resubmitted without penalty, but there are no reveal, hide, or re-request controls because codes are never issued.

14.why: The error message is non-blaming but merely states failure without explaining how to fix it, even though the helper text says the entered demo details are the correct ones.

15.why: No countdown or reading time limit appears on the sign-in screens, but the flow never reaches code entry so generous code-entry time cannot be observed.
